verses.zh: （大卫的诗。）耶和华啊，与我相争的，求你与他们相争！与我相战的，求你与他们相战！
verses.en: By David.O Lord, fight[NOTE:1] those who fight with me.Attack those who attack me.
notes: Psalm 35. The author, who faces ruthless enemies who seek his life for no reason, begs the Lord to fight his battles for him and to vindicate him by annihilating his adversaries.

verses.zh: 拿着大小的盾牌，起来帮助我。
verses.en: Grab your small shield and large shield,[NOTE:1] and rise up to help me.
notes: Or “contend.”

verses.zh: 抽出枪来，挡住那追赶我的；求你对我的灵魂说：我是拯救你的。
verses.en: Use your spear and lance[NOTE:1] against[NOTE:2] those who chase me.Assure me with these words:[NOTE:3] “I am your deliverer.”
notes: Two different types of shields are mentioned here. See also Ezek 38:4. Many modern translations render the first term (translated here “small shield”) as “buckler” (cf. NASB “buckler and shield”; the order is often reversed in the translation, apparently for stylistic reasons: cf. NEB, NIV84, NRSV “shield and buckler”). The English term “buckler,” referring to a small round shield held on the arm to protect the upper body, is unfamiliar to many modern readers, so the term “small shield” was used in the present translation for clarity.
Or “javelin.” On the meaning of this word, which occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible, see M. Dahood, Psalms (AB), 1:210-11.
Heb “draw out spear and lance to meet.”

verses.zh: 愿那寻索我命的，蒙羞受辱！愿那谋害我的，退后羞愧！
verses.en: May those who seek my life be embarrassed and humiliated.May those who plan to harm me be turned back and ashamed.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “say to me,” or “say to my soul.”

verses.zh: 愿他们像风前的糠，有耶和华的使者赶逐他们。
verses.en: May they be[NOTE:1] like wind-driven chaff,as the angel of the Lord[NOTE:2] attacks them.[NOTE:3]
notes: The four prefixed verbal forms in this verse are understood as jussives. The psalmist is calling judgment down on his enemies. See also the distinct jussive form in v. 6.
The prefixed verbal form is taken as a jussive. See v. 4.
See the mention of the angel of the Lord in Ps 34:7.

verses.zh: 愿他们的道路又暗又滑，有耶和华的使者追赶他们。
verses.en: May their path be[NOTE:1] dark and slippery,as the angel of the Lord chases them.
notes: Heb “as the angel of the Lord pushes [them].”

verses.zh: 因他们无故地为我暗设网罗，无故地挖坑，要害我的性命。
verses.en: I did not harm them, but they hid a net to catch meand dug a pit to trap me.[NOTE:1]
notes: The prefixed verbal form is distinctly jussive, indicating this is a prayer.

verses.zh: 愿灾祸忽然临到他身上！愿他暗设的网缠住自己！愿他落在其中遭灾祸！
verses.en: Let destruction take them by surprise.[NOTE:1] Let the net they hid catch them.Let them fall into destruction.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for without cause they hid for me a pit of their net, without cause they dug for my life.” It appears that the words “pit” and “net” have been transposed. “Net” goes with the verb “hid” in the first line (see v. 8, as well as Pss 9:15; 31:4), while “pit” goes with the verb “dug” in the second line (see Ps 7:15).

Heb “let destruction [which] he does not know come to him.” The singular is used of the enemy in v. 8, probably in a representative or collective sense. The psalmist has more than one enemy, as vv. 1-7 make clear.

verses.zh: 我的心必靠耶和华快乐，靠他的救恩高兴。
verses.en: Then I will rejoice in the Lordand be happy because of his deliverance.[NOTE:1]
notes: The psalmist’s prayer for his enemies’ demise continues. See vv. 4-6.

verses.zh: 我的骨头都要说：耶和华啊，谁能像你救护困苦人脱离那比他强壮的，救护困苦穷乏人脱离那抢夺他的？
verses.en: With all my strength I will say,[NOTE:1] “O Lord, who can compare to you?You rescue[NOTE:2] the oppressed from those who try to overpower them,[NOTE:3] the oppressed and needy from those who try to rob them.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “then my soul will rejoice in the Lord and be happy in his deliverance.”
Heb “all my bones will say.”
Heb “[the one who] rescues.” The substantival participle in the Hebrew text characterizes God as one who typically rescues the oppressed.
Heb “from [the one who is] too strong for him.” The singular forms are used in a representative sense. The typical oppressed individual and typical oppressor are in view.

verses.zh: 凶恶的见证人起来，盘问我所不知道的事。
verses.en: Violent men perjure themselves,[NOTE:1] and falsely accuse me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the oppressed [one] and needy [one] from [the one who] robs him.” As in the previous line, the singular forms are used in a representative sense.
Heb “witnesses of violence rise up.”

verses.zh: 他们向我以恶报善，使我的灵魂孤苦。
verses.en: They repay me evil for the good I have done;[NOTE:1] I am overwhelmed with sorrow.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “[that] which I do not know they ask me.”
Heb “they repay me evil instead of good.”

verses.zh: 至于我，当他们有病的时候，我便穿麻衣，禁食，刻苦己心；我所求的都归到自己的怀中。
verses.en: When they were sick, I wore sackcloth,[NOTE:1] and refrained from eating food.[NOTE:2] (If I am lying, may my prayers go unanswered.)[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “[there is] bereavement to my soul.”
Heb “as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth.” Sackcloth was worn by mourners. When the psalmist’s enemies were sick, he was sorry for their misfortune and mourned for them.
Fasting was also a practice of mourners. By refraining from normal activities, such as eating food, the mourner demonstrated the sincerity of his sorrow.

verses.zh: 我这样行，好像他是我的朋友，我的弟兄；我屈身悲哀，如同人为母亲哀痛。
verses.en: I mourned for them as I would for a friend or my brother.[NOTE:1] I bowed down[NOTE:2] in sorrow as if I were mourning for my mother.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and my prayer upon my chest will return.” One could translate, “but my prayer was returning upon my chest,” but the use of the imperfect verbal form sets this line apart from the preceding and following lines (vv. 13a, 14), which use the perfect to describe the psalmist’s past actions.
Heb “like a friend, like a brother to me I walked about.”
I bowed down. Bowing down was a posture for mourning. See Ps 38:6.

verses.zh: 我在患难中，他们却欢喜，大家聚集。我所不认识的那些下流人聚集攻击我；他们不住地把我撕裂。
verses.en: But when I stumbled, they rejoiced and gathered together;they gathered together to ambush me.[NOTE:1] They tore at me without stopping to rest.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “like mourning for a mother [in] sorrow I bowed down.”

Heb “they gathered together against me, stricken [ones], and I did not know.” The Hebrew form נֵכִים (nekhim, “stricken ones” ?) is problematic. Some suggest an emendation to נָכְרִים[כְ] (kenokherim, “foreigners”) or “like foreigners,” which would fit with what follows, “[like] foreigners that I do not recognize.” Perhaps the form should be read as a Qal active participle, נֹכִים (nokhim, “ones who strike”) from the verbal root נָכָה (nakhah, “to strike”). The Qal of this verb is unattested in biblical Hebrew, but the peal (basic) stem appears in Old Aramaic (J. Fitzmyer, The Aramaic Inscriptions of Sefire [BibOr], 114; DNWSI 1:730.) In this case one might translate, “attackers gathered together against me though I was not aware of it” (cf. NASB “smiters”; NEB, NRSV “ruffians”; NIV84 “attackers”; NIV11 “assailants”).

verses.zh: 他们如同席上好嬉笑的狂妄人向我咬牙。
verses.en: When I tripped, they taunted me relentlessly,[NOTE:1] and tried to bite me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “they tore and did not keep quiet.” By using the verb “tear,” the psalmist likens his enemies to a wild animal (see Hos 13:8). In v. 17 he compares them to hungry young lions.

The MT reads “as profane [ones] of mockers of food,” which is difficult. The present translation assumes (1) an emendation of בְּחַנְפֵי (bekhanfe, “as profane men”) to בְּחַנְפִי (bekhanfi, “when I tripped”; preposition + Qal infinitive construct from II חָנַף [“limp”] + first common singular pronominal suffix) and (2) an emendation of לַעֲגֵי מָעוֹג (laʿage maʿog, “mockers of food”) to עָגוּ [ם]לַעְגָּ (laʿgam ʿagu, “[with] taunting they taunted”; masculine plural noun with enclitic mem + Qal perfect third common plural from לַּעַג [laʿag, “taunt”]).

verses.zh: 主啊，你看着不理要到几时呢？求你救我的灵魂脱离他们的残害！救我的生命（生命：原文是独一者）脱离少壮狮子！
verses.en: O Lord, how long are you going to watch this? Rescue[NOTE:1] me[NOTE:2] from their destructive attacks;guard my life[NOTE:3] from the young lions.
notes: Heb “gnashing at me with their teeth.” The infinitive absolute adds a complementary action—they gnashed with their teeth as they taunted.
Heb “bring back, restore.”
Or “my life.”

verses.zh: 我在大会中要称谢你，在众民中要赞美你。
verses.en: Then I will give you thanks in the great assembly;[NOTE:1] I will praise you before a large crowd of people.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “my only one.” The psalmist may mean that his life is precious, or that he feels isolated and alone (see Ps 22:20). The verb “guard” is supplied in the translation because the verb “rescue” is understood by ellipsis (see the previous line).
The great assembly is also mentioned in Ps 22:25.

verses.zh: 求你不容那无理与我为仇的向我夸耀！不容那无故恨我的向我挤眼！
verses.en: Do not let those who are my enemies for no reason[NOTE:1] gloat[NOTE:2] over me.Do not let those who hate me without cause carry out their wicked schemes.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “among numerous people.”
Heb “[with] a lie.” The Hebrew noun שֶׁקֶר (sheqer, “lie”) is used here as an adverb, “falsely, wrongfully” (see Ps 38:19).
Heb “rejoice.”

verses.zh: 因为他们不说和平话，倒想出诡诈的言语害地上的安静人。
verses.en: For they do not try to make peace with others,[NOTE:1] but plan ways to deceive those who live peacefully in the land.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “[do not let] those who hate me without cause pinch [i.e., wink] an eye.” The negative particle is understood in the second line by ellipsis (see the preceding line). In the Book of Proverbs “winking an eye” is associated with deceit and trickery (see 6:13; 10:10; 16:30).
Heb “for they do not speak peace.”

verses.zh: 他们大大张口攻击我，说：阿哈，阿哈，我们的眼已经看见了！
verses.en: They are ready to devour me;[NOTE:1] they say, “Aha! Aha! We’ve got you!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “but against the quiet ones of the land words of deceit they plan.” The imperfect verbal forms in v. 20 highlight their characteristic behavior.

Heb “and they cause their mouth to be wide against me.” The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) consecutive here carries on the generalizing mood of the previous verse. For other examples of this use of the prefixed verbal form with vav consecutive, see GKC 329 §111.t.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你已经看见了，求你不要闭口！主啊，求你不要远离我！
verses.en: But you take notice,[NOTE:1] Lord; do not be silent!O Lord, do not remain far away from me.
notes: Heb “our eye sees.” Apparently this is an idiom meaning to “look in triumph” or “gloat over” (see Ps 54:7).

verses.zh: 我的　神我的主啊，求你奋兴醒起，判清我的事，伸明我的冤！
verses.en: Rouse yourself, wake up[NOTE:1] and vindicate me.[NOTE:2] My God and Lord, defend my just cause.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “you see, O Lord.” There is a deliberate play on words. In v. 21 the enemies say, “our eye sees,” but the psalmist is confident that the Lord “sees” as well, so he appeals to him for help (see also v. 17).
Though he is confident that the Lord is aware of his situation (see v. 22a), the psalmist compares the Lord’s inactivity to sleep and urges him to wake up.
Heb “for my justice.”

verses.zh: 耶和华―我的　神啊，求你按你的公义判断我，不容他们向我夸耀！
verses.en: Vindicate me by your justice, O Lord my God.Do not let them gloat[NOTE:1] over me.
notes: Heb “for my cause.”

verses.zh: 不容他们心里说：阿哈，遂我们的心愿了！不容他们说：我们已经把他吞了！
verses.en: Do not let them say to themselves,[NOTE:1] “Aha! We have what we wanted!”[NOTE:2] Do not let them say, “We have devoured him.”
notes: Heb “rejoice.”
Heb “in their heart[s].”

verses.zh: 愿那喜欢我遭难的一同抱愧蒙羞！愿那向我妄自尊大的披惭愧，蒙羞辱！
verses.en: May those who rejoice in my troubles be totally embarrassed and ashamed.[NOTE:1] May those who arrogantly taunt me be covered with shame and humiliation.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Aha! Our desire!” The “desire” of the psalmist’s enemies is to triumph over him.
Heb “may they be embarrassed and ashamed together, the ones who rejoice over my harm.”

verses.zh: 愿那喜悦我冤屈得伸的（冤屈得伸：原文是公义）欢呼快乐；愿他们常说：当尊耶和华为大！耶和华喜悦他的仆人平安。
verses.en: May those who desire my vindication shout for joy and rejoice.May they continually say,[NOTE:1] “May the Lord be praised,[NOTE:2] for he wants his servant to be secure.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “may they be clothed with shame and humiliation, the ones who magnify [themselves] against me.” The prefixed verbal forms in v. 26 are understood as jussives (see vv. 24b-25, where the negative particle אַל (ʾal) appears before the prefixed verbal forms, indicating they are jussives). The psalmist is calling down judgment on his enemies.
The prefixed verbal forms in v. 27a are understood as jussives (see vv. 24b-26).
The prefixed verbal form is taken as a jussive, “may the Lord be magnified [in praise].” Another option is to take the verb as an imperfect, “the Lord is great.”

verses.zh: 我的舌头要终日论说你的公义，时常赞美你。
verses.en: Then I will tell others about your justice,[NOTE:1] and praise you all day long.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the one who desires the peace of his servant.”
Heb “and my tongue will proclaim your justice.”
